entries.reason: R1 — src/flow/lib/review-failure.js defines a ReviewFailure taxonomy with all five required classifications and separates provider/input-size/max-attempts/verdict/subprocess handling.; R2 — run-review now classifies subprocess failures via ReviewFailure, uses shouldRetrySubprocess for retry decisions, does not retry signal/killed or input size/provider classifications, and caps mechanical retryCount to 2 retries/3 total attempts.; R3 — Provider/input-size failures use retryBudgetConsumed=false, return envelope data with required fields, persist matching reviewStop data, and return before reviewRetry is incremented.; R4 — REVIEW_MAX_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED now builds ReviewFailure.maxAttemptsExceeded and returns toEnvelopeData containing phase, attempts, max, and recoveryCommand while preserving existing fields.; R5 — get-next-action now builds a reviewStop view from flow.json reviewStop or reviewRetry metrics for review steps and projects stopReason, classification, retryBudgetConsumed, and recoveryCommand into the result.; R6 — get-status now derives reviewStop for the active review step from persisted reviewStop or reviewRetry metrics and includes a status summary plus recoveryCommand in the status output.; R9 — review.js catch path classifies provider/input-size errors via ReviewFailure.fromMessage and emits one stderr marker line with classification, reason, recoveryHint, and recoveryCommand; ReviewFailure marker parsing supports structured marker classification for run-review.; R7 — Task review prompt explicitly states task-scope is a non-CLI-enforced soft limit from next-action maxAttempts, notes current default 1, and distinguishes it from flow-scope CLI enforcement.; R8 — CLI-facing review guidance explicitly says not to add issue-log entries solely for provider/input-size failures and to record only for workaround, specification decision changes, or unresolved manual recovery; helper requiresIssueLog encodes the same policy.; Spec Test Coverage — The diff adds test code under specs/258-review-retry-recovery/tests/ and the test file starts with a // spec: R1 R2 R3 R4 R5 R6 R7 R8 R9 header.;
